result.rationale: In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff passes `credentialId` as refreshOAuthTokens' third (userId) parameter — `"zoho-bigin", credentialId` — while every other integration (google, hubspot, lark, office365, zoom, zohocrm, webex) passes `credential.userId`. refreshOAuthTokens serializes that argument as `calcomUserId` to the credential-sync endpoint, so Bigin would send the credential's DB id instead of the user id, breaking credential sync for Bigin (wrong/nonexistent user resolution).

judged_text: Bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential's DB id) as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter — which is serialized as `calcomUserId` in the sync request — while every other app passes credential.userId. The credential-sync endpoint receives a credential id where the Cal.com user id is required, so it resolves the wrong or a nonexistent user and Zoho Bigin credential sync fails (or syncs the wrong user's token) even after the response-shape handling is fixed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call to `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, whereas all other integrations in the diff pass `credential.userId` (e.g. hubspot/lark/zoom/etc.). Given `refreshOAuthTokens`’s signature `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` and that it serializes this value as `calcomUserId` in the sync request body, sending a credential DB id instead of the Cal.com user id will cause the credential-sync endpoint to look up the wrong/nonexistent user and break or misapply token refresh syncing for Zoho Bigin.
